what_happened: suite_selection_select maps ANY path whose basename is README.md -- including specs/evidence/<slug>/README.md -- to a 17-suite agent-system shell-suite list, purely on the basename. A plan phase whose only touched path is such a README therefore cannot honestly claim the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel, even though every one of those suites is irrelevant to a specs/** markdown file. validate-artifact.sh caught the false sentinel claim at authoring time (good), then caught a partial suite-naming reword as an under-verification warning; the shape that passes is a Tier Justification that names the prose diff read-through as the covering check and describes the suite list without naming individual suites. Worth knowing before any future plan tiers a specs/** README phase.

Reading context/project/lean4/patterns/plan-authoring-gate-collisions.md BEFORE decomposing (the domain plan-authoring-gotcha query) directly determined this plan's phase split. Condition 1 establishes that ANY Lean line-count change -- including a pure docstring edit, which is exactly this plan's expected deliverable -- moves typst/generated/status.typ, which .githooks/pre-commit enforces as commit-BLOCKING. Without that read, the docstring phase's own commit would have been refused. The regeneration is scheduled inside the same phase that moves the count, and the two non-blocking inventory surfaces are deferred to the final phase.

Per-site attribution inside one file: setting 'profiler true' in both A/B arms makes Lean report 'tactic execution of ... decide took' and 'type checking took' once per declaration in source order, so the certA and small-witness sites are separable from the same run. This kept the harness at the plan's declared three files instead of needing a separate file per site per arm, and gave a kernel-only column (type checking) distinct from elaboration-time whnf.

A 3-pass-per-arm batch (the plan's stated sample size) gave r_certA=0.863 and r_witness=0.810 -- NEW apparently 14-19 percent faster at both sites. A 10-pass batch under the same lock and build did not reproduce that margin: r_certA=0.984, r_witness=1.055. Within-arm spread is ~20 percent, so three passes is too few to separate a real margin from noise. Both batches are recorded in the evidence README rather than keeping only the flattering one; both agree on D1's question (neither ratio near 1.15).

The certA backward fixpoint now costs ~0.88 s per arm under the kernel, against the 25.9/24.4 s the original A/B recorded -- roughly 30x faster, through intervening work that is not the hoist. The measurement reproduces the original VERDICT (neutral) but not its absolute scale, so any future reader comparing the two records must read the ratio and not the seconds.

Phase 3 ran with no friction: the plan scheduled scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix inside the same phase that moves the line count and carried typst/generated/status.typ in that phase's own file scope, so the commit-blocking generated surface was already reconciled when the commit fired. The plan's scope hypothesis (Tab family has zero references outside LiveFix.lean) was confirmed exactly: all 27 references are in that one file.

The dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral asked for a narrowing invocation (run-all.sh --only SUITE or verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N) covering this phase's touched files, but neither can express them: every verify-deploy.sh gate compares a deployed .claude/ tree against its source store, and this record touched nothing under .claude/ or agent-system/; run-all.sh's suites exercise agent-system shell scripts, not the Lean library. This is the directive's UNMAPPABLE CRITERION branch. Discharged by running the repo checks that do cover these files directly -- check-module-invariants.sh (55 PASS, 0 FAIL), typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only, full lake build, and the task-reference and record-versioning lints per touched deliverable -- and recording that as the scoped discharge.
